context_note: Headline pooled result. Brazil only (tropical + subtropical), 53 studies / 826 observations, field experiments 1988-2023. Control = fallow OR a previous off-season cash crop (e.g., maize, wheat), so this is a mixed baseline. Effect on the soybean crop that follows. Q df = 52, so the pooling is at study level. I2 = 91%. Soybean only: the paper reports no corn yield effect of its own.

issue: This restates E1 in absolute terms (8.7% x 3.30 Mg/ha baseline). It is not an independent result. value_kind 'stock difference' is the wrong label.

Subgroup by control type (Fig. 4a): cover crop vs fallow. Best comparable to the usual 'cover crop vs no cover crop' contrast. n and CI are only in the figure.
Subgroup by control type (Fig. 4a): cover crop replacing an off-season cash crop. This is not a no-cover-crop control. Still significant (p. 9).
Climate subgroup (Fig. 3a). Both subgroup means (17.14, 9.01) are larger than the pooled 8.72%, an artefact of subgroup weighting. Do not treat subgroup values as additive or as pooled estimates.
Climate subgroup (Fig. 3a). The subtropical zone is the most comparable to temperate US/EU systems.
Functional-group subgroup (Fig. 4b). Grasses here are largely Urochloa/millet in tropical systems.
Functional-group subgroup (Fig. 4b). Grass+legume mixtures 8.62%, other types 4.01%.

Meta-regression slope (y = 2.61x - 5.9, R2 = 0.12, n = 261 observations, grass biomass about 0.5-18 Mg/ha). This is a rate, not a mean effect, so do not pool it with the percent effects. The legume biomass relation was not significant (n = 57).
